inferences: Guard work is material: approximately 61-66% of each 20ms packet budget in measured wall time, and about 35-38% of one CPU core if called 50 times per second, before additional events/backpressure retries.

In this separate synthetic process, average guard-only throughput is approximately 76-81 checks per second, above 50 packets per second. This by itself does not establish that SQL causes all 840 output underruns.
Fifteen to twenty percent of individual checks exceed 20ms, with a 35-40ms maximum. Tail latency and other producer/GTK/barge work can erode buffering margin.

Eight dependencies were not slower on average than one in this run. These results do not identify per-source SELECT count as the dominant component; connection setup, OS scheduling and other shared load remain plausible contributors.

The script ran as a separate process alongside existing UI/listening/camera, without models/playback or the real database. The actual GUI producer also shares its own GIL and event loop; its cost may differ.
first_chunk_emitted_ms is measured after the entire first sentence is queued. The observed sink span and prepare_total include 128-entry queue backpressure and cannot be treated as pure SQL CPU time.
decision: Keep the current guard unchanged for root's single-variable half-duplex validation (disable generation/playback barge capture). If starvation persists, measure/implement a separately reviewed anonymous single fresh-read transaction and batched dependency query, preserving every-packet and post-wait invalidation checks.
